lines: Your brain has about 86 billion neurons. AI copied the idea... using nothing but numbers.
This is a neural network. Let's teach one to spot a cat.
A photo goes in as millions of tiny numbers: pixels.
Each artificial neuron takes in numbers, multiplies each one by a weight, and adds them up.
If the total is big enough, it fires, passing a signal to the next layer.
Early layers spot simple edges. Deeper layers combine them into ears, eyes, and whiskers.
But at first, the weights are random. So it guesses... toaster.
We measure how wrong it was, then nudge every weight a tiny bit to shrink the error.
This is called backpropagation. Repeat it millions of times, and the network learns.
Nobody programmed the rules. It found them... by making mistakes.
